title: Library Access
text: The university library supports students, teachers, and approved researchers. Students use their university card to enter and borrow books. A student may borrow up to three books at one time. The normal borrowing period is fourteen days. A book can be renewed once if nobody else has requested it. Reference books, newspapers, and the latest journal issues must be used inside the library. The library opens from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. On Saturday, it opens from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. It is closed on Sunday and public holidays. During examination weeks, the university may announce longer hours. Students should check official notices for temporary changes. A late fine may apply when a book is returned after its due date. Students can check borrowed items and due dates at the circulation desk. Lost or damaged books should be reported to library staff. The library provides quiet study areas, group rooms, computers, and internet access. Group rooms should be booked in advance. Food is not allowed near books or computers. Students should keep phones silent and respect other readers.

title: Campus IT Help Desk
text: The campus IT help desk assists students and staff with university technology services. It can help with account access, password resets, campus Wi-Fi, printing, and classroom computers. Before asking for support, users should note the device type, when the problem started, and any error message. The help desk is available Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Users can submit a request through the university portal or visit the IT office. Requests are handled according to urgency. A classroom outage during a scheduled lesson is urgent because it affects teaching. Optional software installation is normally lower priority. Users must never send their password by email or chat. IT staff will not ask for a complete password. Suspicious messages should be reported without opening their links. Multi-factor authentication should remain enabled. For Wi-Fi problems, users should check that Wi-Fi is switched on and that they selected the official campus network. Restarting the device may solve a temporary issue. If the problem continues, submit the device details and location. The help desk may ask the user to visit the IT office for further checks.

title: Programming Lab
text: Students using the programming laboratory must follow the lab rules. They should sign in with their own account and save work in the folder assigned by the instructor. Students must not share account passwords. Before leaving, they should save their files, sign out, and leave the workstation ready for the next class. Programming assignments are submitted through the learning management system unless the instructor gives a different instruction. A submission should include source code and any required report. File names should identify the student and assignment. Students should open uploaded files after submission to confirm that the correct versions were received. Code should be readable and include comments where the purpose of a section is not obvious. Students are encouraged to test programs with normal inputs, boundary values, and invalid inputs. If a program fails, the report should describe the error and investigation steps. Copying another student's work without permission is not acceptable. Food and drinks should be kept away from computers. Hardware faults should be reported to the lab assistant. Students must not install unapproved software or change system settings.

title: Academic Advising
text: The student support office helps learners understand academic procedures and find university services. Students may ask about course registration, timetable questions, academic advising, and general study support. The office can explain published procedures, but it cannot promise that a request will be approved. Decisions requiring academic authority are referred to the relevant department. Students should bring university identification when visiting. For an academic advising meeting, they should prepare their course list and write down questions they want to discuss. This helps the meeting focus on actual needs. If a student cannot attend an appointment, they should contact the office early. The support office handles personal information carefully. Students should use official university channels when sending documents. They should not post private records in public groups. Staff may need to confirm identity before discussing account-specific information. Opening hours are Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The office may close during university holidays. Students should check current notices before travelling to campus. For urgent safety concerns, contact campus security or local emergency services rather than waiting for a routine appointment.

title: Project Room Booking
text: Students may reserve a project room for supervised group work, presentations, and approved academic activities. A booking request should include the group name, requested date, start time, end time, expected number of participants, and responsible student's name. Requests should be submitted through the campus room booking portal. A room is not reserved until the portal displays a confirmation. Sending a request does not guarantee availability. If the requested room is already booked, the system may show another room or time. Students should check confirmation details and keep the booking reference. If plans change, the responsible student should cancel the reservation so another group can use it. The responsible student should arrive on time and leave the room tidy. Projectors and whiteboards should be used carefully. Damage or technical issues should be reported to campus facilities. The room must not be used for activities outside the approved purpose. Bookings are normally limited to two hours per group per day. Longer sessions require department approval. Rooms may be unavailable during examinations, maintenance, or official events. The booking portal is the official source for room availability.
